questions.q: After a DNS record is updated for a migration, some users still see the old server for hours. What's the likely cause?
options: The load balancer failed its health check
The firewall is blocking the new server
Some resolvers are still serving a cached answer because the TTL wasn't lowered beforehand
The new server is down
questions.explain: If the TTL wasn't lowered before the migration, some resolvers keep serving the old cached answer until it naturally expires.

questions.q: A site starts showing a browser security warning with no recent deployment. What's a likely cause?
options: The TLS certificate expired
A load balancer health check is failing
The DNS record changed
A port-forwarding rule was removed
questions.explain: A quietly expired certificate causes exactly this symptom — a security warning on an otherwise unchanged, healthy server.

questions.q: After tightening a security group, a load balancer starts marking all backends unhealthy. What's the likely cause?
options: The certificate expired
The new rule is blocking the load balancer's own health-check traffic
DNS TTL was set too low
The backend servers ran out of disk space
questions.explain: A security group change made right before the symptom appeared is the strongest clue — it likely blocked the health-check traffic itself.

questions.q: What's the telltale sign of an overloaded backend rather than a misconfiguration?
options: Every request fails identically every time
Failures are intermittent and correlate with load, while the service mostly still works
DNS stops resolving the domain
The server stops responding to ping entirely
questions.explain: An overloaded service is still functioning but can't keep up with demand, producing intermittent, load-correlated failures rather than a clean, total failure.

questions.q: What do all four failure scenarios in this lesson have in common?
options: They can all be diagnosed using the same bottom-up methodology and tools from the previous lessons
They all require replacing the server
They all require a new certificate
They only occur in cloud environments
questions.explain: Despite different root causes, each scenario is solvable with the same bottom-up approach and the same ping/traceroute/dig/curl/ss toolkit.
